name: loupixdeck-companion
description: Connects Visual Studio Code to the LoupixDeck plugin: run any command from a deck key and see live problems, git, debug, task and editor state on the deck.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The command policy is read from user settings only, so a workspace cannot loosen it.

loupixdeck.enabled.markdownDescription: Run the local server that the LoupixDeck plugin connects to. Turn it off to disconnect this editor from the deck.

enumDescriptions: The deck may run any command.
The deck may run only the commands listed in `#loupixdeck.allowedCommands#`.
loupixdeck.commandPolicy.markdownDescription:
Which commands the deck may run.

The companion listens on a socket that only your user account can open (a Unix socket in a private folder, or a named pipe on Windows), and every connection must present a random token from a file only you can read. Nothing listens on the network. Any program running as you can read that token, just as it could already run anything else as you.

`allowList` refuses every command not listed in `#loupixdeck.allowedCommands#`. Running tasks and launch configurations from the deck's folders, and bringing the window to the front, stay allowed.

Only your user settings count: a workspace's `.vscode/settings.json` cannot change this.

loupixdeck.allowedCommands.markdownDescription: Command IDs the deck may run when `#loupixdeck.commandPolicy#` is `allowList`, for example `workbench.action.files.save`.

loupixdeck.pushDiagnostics.markdownDescription: Push problem counts to the deck as they change. In very large workspaces with constant diagnostics churn, turn this off; the deck then reads the counts only when it connects or asks.
